notes:
Qualification summary:
- Target: enterprise healthcare analytics platform; heavy PHI, must keep data in EU (DE/FR/IE regions)
- Primary interest: Redwood Private (VPC) with customer-managed KMS and audit log forwarding to Splunk/QRadar.
- Current infra: hybrid AWS (eu-west-1 primary) + on-prem VMware in Frankfurt for legacy EHR connectors.
Security and compliance highlights:
- Must support SSO (SAML) + SCIM for provisioning.
- KMS: customer holds keys (AWS KMS CMKs) and requires HSM-backed attestation for key usage. Explicit no-escrow unless legal secures.
- Audit: full request/response audit trails, token-level cost attribution useful but all telemetry must be exportable to existing SIEM.
- Residency: data-at-rest + model KV cache must never leave EU. Concern about fallback routing to non-EU regions.
Architecture fit notes (from SE call 2024-11-05):
- Prefer private control plane that can be deployed with VPC peering or PrivateLink.
- VPC topology: recommended pattern is single-managed Redwood subnet for workers, customer-managed NATs for controlled egress, and dedicated ENIs for private control plane. They flagged inbound restrictions:
  - Inbound: minimal; only established connections from control plane to MGMT network via PrivateLink.
  - Outbound: strict egress rules; telemetry + S3 backups must go to approved endpoints (whitelist).
- Sequence length/workload: many short chat sessions (clinical triage) + periodic large-batch embeddings for nightly indexing. Throughput target ~200 req/s with p50 latency < 150ms for chat.
POC / evaluation plan:
- POC requested: 3-week private deployment in their AWS account (eu-central-1) with sample EHR dataset (anonymized).
- Milestones: network design sign-off -> KMS integration test -> audit log ingestion test -> load test (200rps) -> security review signoff.
